TMP-0735.text: CASE STUDY Ordinary Habit Juan Roballo/Alamy Stock Photo Pricing strategy is a puzzle for any business. Online retailers feel the forces of competition, with countless stores of every imaginable type of product just a few clicks away. The ease of shopping and comparing prices challenges online stores to differentiate their products and choose prices wisely. The Ordinary Habit puzzle store successfully navigated the internet’s ocean of competition when the waters were particularly rough.

TMP-0736.text: Founded in 2019 by mother–daughter duo Teresa and Echo Hopkins, Ordinary Habit began with a simple purpose: “to create artful objects, designed to be both fun and functional, that would help people access habitual moments of calm and connectedness.” 2 Armed with a strong belief in the transformative nature of “daily play,” these entrepreneurs endeavored to create a debut product that would stand out with its beauty, sustainability, and simplicity of use. To make delivery fast and efficient, they sought a product that was easy to transport. And with an instinctive understanding of Cialdini’s scarcity principle (as discussed in Module 2.2 ), which states that people value rare items, they were drawn to an item with restricted supply. They settled on a series of limited-edition jigsaw puzzles that would function both as a reason to get together with friends and a path to “peace and time away from the digital world.” They launched their first puzzle during the COVID-19 pandemic, when people were looking for fun things to do at home. It was an opportune time for puzzle makers. Google searches for puzzles saw a 671% increase at the start of the shutdown in March 2020. One of the world’s top puzzle manufacturers, Ravensburger, reported that its puzzle sales increased by 370% in March 2020 from

TMP-0737.text: March 2019. 3 With striking puzzle images and boxes designed to look like artwork, Ordinary Habit achieved early success. It has since expanded its collection to include matching cards and “on the go” games. Its product differentiation included offering a product made in an ethical way. Ordinary Habit struggled initially to find a manufacturer that understood its vision for a unique product made only with recycled materials. After many meetings, the company finally struck up a relationship with a woman-owned manufacturing business in Poland that provided exactly such a puzzle, artfully designed and made entirely of recycled materials. With a manufacturer secured and product samples in hand, the company needed a pricing strategy. The internet brought consumers to a host of puzzle options, but Ordinary Habit provided no ordinary puzzle. With its product differentiation, it could charge more than sellers of ordinary puzzles. However, if the company charged a higher price than other sellers of premium puzzles, it could expect to lose a disproportionately large number of sales to the competition. Ordinary Habit chose a price of $20 for its 100-piece puzzles, a competitive pricing strategy that put its price in line with rivals Crocodile Creek, Serious Puzzles, and the Hopscotch

TMP-0738.text: Children’s Store. Ordinary Habit also adopted bundle pricing , offering multiple puzzles for less than the combined price of the individual puzzles. Teresa and Echo Hopkins built their company on the belief that active minds cultivate meaningful change. Thanks to their thoughtful product design, marketing, pricing, and distribution, the duo has changed many lives for the better with their products—and they do even more with their earnings. They have pledged to donate a percentage of their profit to groups that support emotional health and well-being, such as the Loveland Foundation, which provides access to mental health resources for Black women and girls. Ordinary Habit anticipates continued growth and plans to introduce new products that celebrate daily play while fostering small moments of mindfulness. Apply Your AP ® Skills 1. Identify three ways that this company differentiates its product from the average puzzle. 2. How would you describe the type of customer Ordinary Habit seems to be targeting?

TMP-0740.text: MODULE 2.6 Place and Channels LG LEARNING GOALS In this module, you will learn to: 2.6.A Explain the various distribution channels available to businesses 2.6.B Explain how a business chooses a distribution channel

TMP-0741.text: When a business chooses its distribution channel, it must decide whether to use intermediaries such as wholesalers and retailers. Slate Auto decided to sell directly to its customers rather than having traditional car dealerships as intermediaries.

TMP-0742.text: Distribution Channels and Business Models LG What are the ways businesses can get their products to customers? According to an old saying, “The three most important factors for business success are location, location, and location.” In other words, it is crucial to find the right physical location for a business. As one of the 4 Ps of the marketing mix, place has the somewhat broader meaning of where and how a product is made available to customers. Place can be a physical location where customers encounter the product, such as a retail store, a sporting event, a hospital, or a restaurant. It can also be a virtual space, such as an online store or marketplace. place Where and how a product is made available to customers.

TMP-0743.text: The question of place also involves supply-chain decisions about how the product will reach consumers. For goods, businesses must decide what intermediaries—such as distribution centers and retailers—will be involved. For services, dilemmas include whether to deliver the service in person, live online, or recorded online. If place is chosen well, the product will be available to the right customers at the right time in the right location. Choosing the wrong place, even for the right product, leads to lost sales opportunities. Direct and Indirect Channels Place is determined by a business’s choice of a distribution channel (also known as a marketing channel ), which is the way a finished product gets from its producer to its final customer. The distribution channel is the final step in the supply chain, encompassing all of the workers and businesses involved in completing the product’s journey to its ultimate user. distribution channel The way a finished product gets from its producer to its final customer. (Also known as a marketing channel .)

TMP-0744.text: The two general types of distribution channels are direct and indirect. A direct distribution channel is a way for a company to sell goods or services directly to consumers without the use of intermediaries such as wholesalers or retailers. For example, Bombas sells socks and other items directly to consumers. Company-owned retailers such as Apple stores and Tesla showrooms do the same. The Dollar Shave Club delivers razors directly to subscribers. Dell Computers is heavily reliant on direct sales, although, like Apple, it also sells some of its products through other stores such as Best Buy. direct distribution channel A way for a company to sell goods or services directly to consumers without the use of intermediaries such as wholesalers or retailers.

TMP-0745.text: Middleman? Never Met Him. How do we deliver a smooth shave at such a great price? We make our own blades. That's right we cut out the middle man to keep your wallet full. Extended description for Middleman Posed on the desk in front of the man are Dollar Shave Club products, including a razor and shaving cream. Text overlaid on the photo reads, Middleman? Never Met Him. How do we deliver a smooth shave at such a great price? We make our own blades. That's right we cut out the middle man to keep your wallet full.

TMP-0746.text: The Dollar Shave Club launched in 2011 as a subscription service with a direct distribution channel. It delivered razors and other personal grooming products directly to customers by mail. Now it also has indirect distribution channels that sell products through retailers such as Walmart, Meijer, and Amazon. An indirect distribution channel is a way to sell goods or services using intermediaries. For goods, possible intermediaries include wholesalers, retailers, e- commerce platforms, and distributors, as noted in Module 1.8 ’s discussion of supply chains. For services, intermediaries include agents, brokers, and online platforms such as Fiverr and Upwork that connect service workers with clients. indirect distribution channel A way to sell goods or services using intermediaries. Figure 2.6-1 provides a comparison of direct distribution and one scenario for indirect distribution. Companies with indirect distribution can choose among several strategies for how broadly they will make their products available among retailers.

TMP-0749.text: Figure 2.6-1 Direct and Indirect Distribution • With intensive distribution , a company sells through as many retailers as possible. For example, sunglasses are now available at supermarkets, drugstores, and gas stations in addition to stores that specialize in sunglasses. This strategy works well for low-priced products or impulse purchases, such as chewing gum, snacks, and winter hats. • With selective distribution , a company sells through a small number of carefully chosen retailers. This strategy is typically used for selling relatively expensive, high- quality products such as computers, household appliances, and high-end sunglasses such as Oakleys. • With exclusive distribution , a company sells its products through just one retailer. Early on, Ralph Lauren’s men’s line was sold exclusively at Bloomingdale’s department store. Now the brand uses selective distribution. Other examples of exclusive distribution include car brands that are sold only through that brand’s dealerships.

TMP-0750.text: Later in this module, we will discuss the selection of a distribution channel. Like Dell, Apple, and Ralph Lauren, many companies experiment with several distribution channels to find the best fit. Recently, the Ford Motor Company has experimented with direct sales in addition to sales through independently owned dealerships. As we’ll discuss next, there are also decisions to be made about whether to make products for individuals or for other businesses. Service Delivery As with goods, the place where services are delivered matters to customers. People will pay for music on their phones, but they will pay more to hear the same music live in a dingy bar and even more to hear the same music in the Red Rocks Amphitheatre in Colorado. Similarly, medical services, training programs, theater performances, financial services, customer service, and counseling are among the services that can be delivered in many different places in many ways. Transportation services can be provided by taxi services, public transportation, ride-hailing apps like Lyft, car rental services, planes, trains, or bicycles. Even meal services can be dine-in, take-out, delivered from services like DoorDash, or mail ordered from services such as Blue Apron.

TMP-0751.text: In-person service delivery can provide a better customer experience, but it is expensive because the provider must either go to the customer or create a place of business that is welcoming to customers. Prerecorded services such as education or entertainment delivered on electronic devices are inexpensive, but impersonal. Live online services provide a middle ground, allowing for a customized experience while lowering the cost of bringing customers and service providers together. A business must assess its target customers to determine whether their priority is low prices, personal service, or some balance of the two. In the case of singing lessons, there are large enough customer segments with each priority to support all three types of service providers. Some businesses provide in-person singing lessons, some provide prerecorded lessons, and some provide online lessons. Sports fans may watch sporting events in person, on recordings, and live on television using cable or internet streaming services. More and more services, such as healthcare and library services, are innovating with delivery options that involve various forms of technology and artificial intelligence. The future holds service delivery processes we can only imagine.

TMP-0752.text: John P Kelly/Getty Images How services are delivered matters. The same music available on your phone is more valuable if experienced live and in-person—especially if it’s in a beautiful setting, such as Colorado’s Red Rocks Amphitheatre. Service providers also face decisions between distribution channels. Some choose a direct distribution channel by providing the service directly to customers without third-

TMP-0753.text: party involvement. Examples include a doctor treating patients in a private practice, a personal trainer offering sessions directly to clients, and Hulu streaming movies directly to subscribers. Other service providers use indirect distribution channels. If you go to a concert or a comedy show, you may find that a third-party intermediary such as Ticketmaster or Eventbrite is handling the sales and distribution of the tickets. Business-to-Business and Business-to- Consumer Sales The businesses most visible to consumers are, naturally, those selling products to consumers, who buy those products and are surrounded by their marketing campaigns. Behind the scenes, however, are millions of businesses in the United States alone that sell their products to other businesses. Before you buy a bike, other businesses sell the bike maker materials and parts such as spokes, tires, brakes, cables, pedals, and metal for the frame. Before you buy a pizza, other businesses sell the pizzeria flour, sauce, and toppings. Businesses selling advertising, office supplies, customer relationship management software, industrial equipment, and commercial loans are among many that cater exclusively to other businesses. In this section, we explore the differences between these businesses and the ones selling to people like you and me.

TMP-0754.text: Business-to-business (B2B) companies sell their goods and services primarily to other businesses. For example, the Oregon-based Bulk Bookstore is a B2B wholesale business that sells books in quantities of 25 or more to other businesses that need them for conferences, large meetings, educational programs, and the like. Business-to- consumer (B2C) companies sell their goods and services primarily to consumers for personal use. The food, clothing, electronics, concert tickets, and other things you buy for yourself come from B2C businesses. business-to-business (B2B) Companies that sell their goods and services primarily to other businesses. business-to-consumer (B2C) Companies that sell their goods and services primarily to consumers for personal use. Some businesses dabble in both B2B and B2C sales. For instance, financial technology company Block, whose products include the customer-focused Cash App digital wallet, started as Square, named after its business-focused system for accepting payments from customers. And online retailer Amazon offers businesses a cloud-based computing platform called Amazon Web Services.

TMP-0755.text: The marketing channels for B2C and B2B businesses differ in important ways. B2C marketing often focuses on visual or emotional appeals. For example, Chobani uses colorful photos on Instagram to show how its yogurt can enhance a Caesar salad, flatbread pizza, or peach cheesecake. In contrast, B2B marketing targets decision makers within businesses who want solutions to problems and a return on their investment. For instance, Helcim advertises its credit card readers with information- rich ads that emphasize low fees and the ability to accept new forms of payment.

TMP-0756.text: Bloomberg/Getty Images Extended description for Docu Sign Text on the screen reads from top to bottom: Sales: 1-877-720-2040. Docu Sign. Free Trial. Send, sign, success. Docu Sign e Signature. Get Started for Free. The eSignature solution trusted by hundreds of (sentence cuts off).

TMP-0757.text: DocuSign is a B2B service sold to businesses such as law firms and real estate agencies to enable their clients to sign documents electronically. The selling process or sales cycle of converting a prospective customer into an actual customer is longer for B2B businesses than for B2C businesses. In B2B, the sales force must appeal to the decision makers in another business. Business customers will typically take more time to make a purchasing decision because they need to carry out research, assess budgets, and study the competition before agreeing to buy. The sales cycle is also longer because the relatively high price of equipment, software, and many other B2B products makes the stakes higher. Building a trusting relationship with a buyer is critical at this stage to make the sale and to secure repeat orders in the future. By contrast, B2C customers typically make smaller purchases and devote less time to the purchase decision. The average consumer is more likely to make purchasing decisions based on “social proof,” such as the recommendations of friends or social media influencers. Unlike B2B customers, who are driven by the goal of enhancing their

TMP-0758.text: business and improving their profits, B2C customers are motivated by desires to improve their lives in some way. They are less data driven and more influenced by emotions, which explains the many consumer advertisements that are light on product information and heavy on emotional content. Table 2.6-1 highlights the differences between B2B and B2C marketing. The contrasts indicate the importance of understanding your target market and focusing on their particular interests. Table 2.6-1 Differences Between B2B and B2C Marketing B2B B2C Target audience Businesses Consumers Who makes the buying decision Managers, professionals, committees All types of individuals Process for obtaining customers Long, complex, often involving negotiation Short, simple, seldom involving negotiation Relationship with buyer Long term, based on trust and relationships with a professional sales team Quick transactions with less personal interaction Bases for decisions Logic, efficiency, budgets, group decisions Emotions, impulses, needs, wants

TMP-0759.text: Volume and pricing Bulk orders, higher-priced items such as equipment and software systems Small orders, lower-priced items such as t-shirts and meals Communication channels Trade shows, webinars, industry publications, experts discussing industry reports and case studies Social media, television, websites, influencers with emotional appeals Distribution channels Industrial distributors, direct sales, websites, B2B marketplaces Retail stores, direct sales, websites, social media platforms, mobile apps

TMP-0760.text: Selecting and Evaluating a Distribution Channel How does a business evaluate and choose the most effective distribution channel for its product? In some cases, the distribution channel is determined by legislation. For instance, prescription drugs must be sold through licensed pharmacies or healthcare providers. Similar laws apply to the sale of alcohol, tobacco, firearms, certain medical devices, hazardous chemicals, aviation equipment, and (where legal) cannabis. However, most businesses have important decisions to make about their distribution channel. In this section, we examine factors relevant to that choice.

TMP-0761.navLabel: Pros and Cons of Direct Channels
TMP-0761.text: Pros and Cons of Direct Channels Key considerations when selecting a distribution channel include cost, control, and consumer perceptions. One advantage of a direct distribution channel is the cost savings achieved by taking intermediaries out of the picture. Distributors, wholesalers, and retailers all want a piece of the profit, leaving less for the producer. The company has more control over pricing and marketing when it handles distribution itself. Customers tend to care about where their products come from and who they are dealing with. Direct distribution connects the business with its customers and strengthens their relationship. And the company’s close ties to consumers allows for direct customer feedback, which makes the business more aware of looming problems. The disadvantages of a direct distribution channel begin with the need for expanded areas of expertise, because the company takes care of all the warehousing, logistics, order fulfillment, and customer service. If the company has weaknesses in these areas, the savings on intermediaries can be swallowed up by higher operational costs. And smaller companies may not reach as many customers on their own as they could if their products were distributed by a large retail firm with stores in every sizable town.

headings.text: Pros and Cons of Direct Channels

TMP-0762.navLabel: Pros and Cons of Indirect Channels
TMP-0762.text: Pros and Cons of Indirect Channels The advantages of an indirect distribution channel include the ability to reach a broader market with the help of intermediaries and their expansive networks of distributors and stores. A purse manufacturer with Macy’s as an intermediary can have its products in hundreds of stores across the country without owning more than a single factory.

headings.text: Pros and Cons of Indirect Channels

TMP-0763.navLabel: Pros and Cons of Indirect Channels
TMP-0763.text: buzbuzzer/Getty Images An advantage of indirect distribution is that the product can be made available in stores across the country, making it more visible and convenient to purchase. The use of relatively efficient intermediaries to warehouse inventory, transport goods, and provide other supply-chain logistics can lower distribution costs for the

TMP-0764.navLabel: Pros and Cons of Indirect Channels
TMP-0764.text: manufacturer. And intermediaries bring expertise to their specialized roles in distribution and sales, allowing manufacturers to focus on product development and production. The disadvantages of an indirect distribution channel include dependency. The use of intermediaries gives companies less control over pricing, customer service, and representation of the brand. When retailers provide a company’s product, they typically control the product displays, inventory management, and customer support, which may not match the manufacturer’s intentions. Profits are spread among the several businesses involved in an indirect distribution channel. The more complicated supply chain may lead to delays or difficulties resolving problems with the product or customer service. And there may be stiff competition for the best intermediaries. For example, it may be difficult for a small purse seller to arrange for Macy’s to sell its products. Given these pros and cons, a business must look inward at its strengths and outward at its customers as it deliberates over the optimal distribution channel. Specifically, the business is wise to consider its abilities to reach its target market, the expertise of its

TMP-0765.navLabel: Pros and Cons of Indirect Channels
TMP-0765.text: employees, its desire for control, and its willingness to share profit. And customers may prefer the convenience of being able to find the product at their local shopping mall, or the comfort of knowing they are dealing directly with the product’s maker. AP ® EXAM TIP An exam question might identify a type of business and ask you to justify the choice of a distribution channel. To prepare, practice explaining the pros and cons of direct and indirect distribution channels.

TMP-0766.text: Module 2.6 Review Learning Goals What are the ways businesses can get their products to customers? The 4 Ps of the marketing mix include place , which is the channel for making the product available and distributing it to consumers. Decisions about place involve the location where customers encounter the product as well as the broader distribution strategy that makes products available to customers. A distribution channel (also known as a marketing channel ) is the way the finished product reaches customers. A direct distribution channel is a way for a company to sell goods or services directly to consumers without the use of intermediaries such as wholesalers or retailers. An indirect distribution channel is a way to sell goods or services using intermediaries.

TMP-0767.text: Business-to-business (B2B) companies sell their goods and services primarily to other businesses. Business-to-consumer (B2C) companies sell their goods and services primarily to consumers for personal use. B2B marketing targets committees and business professionals with information-based appeals. B2C marketing targets individual consumers who make relatively emotional, impulsive purchasing decisions. How does a business evaluate and choose the most effective distribution channel for its product? The advantages of a direct distribution channel include higher profits, increased control, and a closer connection to customers. The disadvantages of a direct distribution channel include higher operational costs, responsibility for order fulfillment, and limited market reach. The advantages of an indirect distribution channel include the ability to reach a broader market, fewer responsibilities for supply-chain logistics, and the ability to draw on the expertise of intermediaries. The disadvantages of an indirect

TMP-0768.text: distribution channel include less control over decisions and a broader sharing of profits. Practice Your AP ® Skills Preparing for the AP ® Exam MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTIONS 1. YT Industries manufactures and sells mountain bikes. Customers purchase YT bikes by visiting YT’s own website or YT’s own store. What type of distribution channel does YT have? a. direct distribution channel b. indirect distribution channel c. intense distribution d. exclusive distribution

TMP-0769.text: 2. Carhartt sells its clothing and gear through a large network of wholesalers and retailers such as Lowe’s and Tractor Supply Company. Which of the following is a clear advantage of this distribution model? a. cost savings b. more control over pricing c. strong connections with customers d. the ability to reach a broader market 3. Which of the following is correct regarding B2B and/or B2C sales? a. B2B sellers typically require less time to acquire customers than B2C sellers. b. B2C consumers are more likely to make decisions based on emotions than are B2B customers, who tend to make data-driven decisions. And as a result, the advertising of B2C sellers tends to be focused on emotional content. c. B2B customers, faced with budget constraints, tend to make smaller purchases than B2C customers. d. B2C customers tend to do more research than B2B customers, which makes the sales cycle longer in B2C sales.

TMP-0770.text: 4. Which statement is correct? a. Companies are always free to choose a direct or indirect distribution channel. b. A disadvantage of selling through indirect distribution channels is that it is generally less efficient to rely on intermediaries to provide supply-chain logistics. c. Customers tend not to care about the source of their products. d. Dependency on intermediaries gives businesses less control over pricing, customer service, and brand representation. 5. Goodyear sells its tires to automobile manufacturers for use in building new cars, and to tire specialty stores such as Big O Tires, where consumers can buy replacement tires for their own cars. This means that Goodyear is a. conducting both B2B and B2C sales. b. conducting only B2B sales. c. conducting only B2C sales. d. conducting neither B2B nor B2C sales.

TMP-0772.text: CASE STUDY The Places for IRONMAN ® Races Xinhua News Agency/Getty Images

TMP-0773.text: Extended description for IRON MAN Hundreds of spectators appear behind the participants, lining the beach far into the distance. Businesses try to put their product in a place where consumers want to go—whether that’s an appealing store, a restaurant, or an online location. For service providers such as the IRONMAN ® Group, the place is a travel destination where consumers will choose to challenge themselves. We’ll investigate that ambitious branch of tourism in the case study for this module. Some products aren’t sold in stores. Services can be provided in homes, medical offices, schools, and online. And sellers in one of the largest industries in the world, tourism, provide their services in cities, jungles, museums, and resorts around the world. Promoters of tours and vacations must choose and develop a place of business so special that buyers will spend large amounts of money to go there for the experience. The IRONMAN ® Group is one such business.

TMP-0774.text: The IRONMAN ® Group is the world’s largest provider of mass participation sports. A typical IRONMAN ® event welcomes about 2,000 competitors. The company also offers several series of shorter triathlons, IRONKIDS ® competitions, the Epic Series of mountain bike races, and the Rock ‘n’ Roll ® Running Series. The IRONMAN ® Group hosts more than 230 events each year in 57 countries with roughly one million participants. Only a small number of competing organizations offer full-distance triathlons like the IRONMAN ® . A “full” IRONMAN ® triathlon consists of a 2.4-mile swim followed by a 112-mile bike ride, and then a 26.2-mile run. The IRONMAN ® Group’s job is to make that into an experience people will pay roughly $750 to endure, not to mention the costs of equipment, travel, and lodging. The marketing team’s first task is to make the event aspirational. Many people love a challenge that leads to feelings of accomplishment and pride. Branding work has made the IRONMAN ® name and logo synonymous with strength and achievement. The “place” question of where customers will access this product is critical. The ideal locations for IRONMAN ® races will draw big crowds willing to pay high prices despite minimal advertising. The IRONMAN ® Group must know its target audience

TMP-0775.text: as it makes tradeoffs between places that are relatively close to many potential customers, convenient, and inexpensive, and places that are more exotic, distant, and pricey. The IRONMAN ® ’s original and most famous location is Hawaii. The company has learned that more people are willing to pay a registration fee that exceeds $1,000 to compete in Hawaii than can be accommodated, and entrants must qualify for that race with an outstanding performance in another IRONMAN ® . Experience taught the IRONMAN ® Group that athletes will travel far and pay extra to compete in places that feel special. Efforts to match locations with customer interests have brought races to Florianópolis, Brazil; Busselton, Australia; Panama City Beach, Florida; and dozens of other far-flung locales. Races have been discontinued in places such as Tulsa, Oklahoma; Louisville, Kentucky; and Penticton, British Columbia. Providers of mass participation sports must also decide whether to have other companies help market and deliver their services. If you sign up for a 5K running race, you may learn about the race, and register on a platform such as RunSignup, RaceHub, or RaceWire. These intermediaries can reach a broader audience than a

TMP-0776.text: local organization putting on a race, and their teams of experts create the online registration portals and payment systems. The IRONMAN ® Group adopted a similar strategy by outsourcing its registration process to TicketSocket, which provides an online platform but allows IRONMAN ® to customize the user interface. This strategy allows consistency across the user experience with marketing, registrations, communications, and events. Ultimately, several types of places matter to what has been called the “racecation” industry. For marketing purposes, the IRONMAN ® Group promotes itself around the world on social media, television broadcasts, emails, and lots and lots of t-shirt logos. Engagement with customers begins on a registration platform, which is such an important place that many race organizers outsource its development to professionals to make sure it stands out. And with athletes willing to pay a high price to test their physical limits in a euphoric setting, businesses in this industry must think carefully about the race place, which is preferably surrounded by palm trees and light breezes.

TMP-0777.text: APPLY YOUR AP ® SKILLS 1. What type of consumer would you target if you were marketing a long-distance triathlon? Explain your answer. 2. If you were hired to extend the reach of the IRONMAN® Group’s marketing efforts, where would you choose to advertise its events? 3. Aside from the physical test and the geographic location, what aspect of the long-distance triathlon market do you think allows the IRONMAN® Group to charge hundreds of dollars or more per race? 4. For a triathlon, the place that arguably matters the most is the actual location of the competition. What are three elements of that place, other than beauty, that you would seek if you were choosing the next location for a triathlon?

TMP-0778.text: MODULE 2.7 Promotion and Marketing Communications LG LEARNING GOALS In this module, you will learn to: 2.7.A Discuss the five elements of the promotional mix 2.7.B Explain what digital tools mean for personalized marketing

TMP-0779.text: TIMOTHY A. CLARY/Getty Images Extended description for Outdoor Advertising The film advertised shows actor Michael Keaton as the character Beetlejuice. Another character with a shrunken head is wearing a sticker that reads, Hello, my name is Bob.

TMP-0780.text: Promotion with outdoor advertising such as bus wraps and billboards has the advantage of reaching a wide swath of people, including those who do not read newspapers or spend much time on social media.

TMP-0781.text: Promoting a Product LG What are the five elements of the promotional mix? When Blizzard Entertainment launched its role-playing action game Diablo IV, it wanted to appeal to current Diablo players and to attract new customers. To do that, the company’s marketing department came up with a strategy that reached around the world to generate excitement. Blizzard’s efforts included a trailer directed by Oscar winner Chloé Zhao, with music by Billie Eilish; scary billboards as far away as South Korea; free game items for qualified KFC customers; a 160-foot mural in a French cathedral; 1 and limited-edition, game-themed “Meat Shakes” delivered to 1,000 fans. The millions of dollars spent on that global campaign paid off. In its first month, Diablo IV had over 10 million players log more than 700 million hours of playing time, setting a sales record for the company. 2

TMP-0782.text: Blizzard had already determined the right product, price, and place, and now it was fully engaged in the fourth P in the marketing mix: promotion , meaning any type of marketing communication used to inform target customers about the product. Promotion is central to a marketing campaign , which is a coordinated effort to publicize a product or build brand awareness and attract new customers. As the Diablo IV example reveals, the possibilities for promotions are vast. The promotional mix is the set of marketing tools a business uses to communicate with potential customers, build brand loyalty, and increase sales. The promotional mix is made up of media advertising, personal selling, sales promotion, direct marketing, and public relations. We’ll discuss reasons and methods for each of these tools next. promotion Any type of marketing communication used to inform target customers about the product. marketing campaign A coordinated effort to publicize a product or build brand awareness and attract new customers. promotional mix The set of marketing tools a business uses to communicate with potential customers, build brand loyalty, and increase sales.

TMP-0783.text: Media Advertising Over 100 million people watch the Super Bowl football game in a typical year. Companies crave a slice of that audience’s attention in the form of a brief advertising spot. Super Bowl ads are an example of media advertising , which is the promotion of goods, services, or brands to a wide audience through channels of mass communication. Those channels, known as media , include print publications, television and radio broadcasts, and outdoor media such as billboards. Media advertising is advisable for a business that wants to reach many potential customers with the same message. Later in this module, we will discuss digital media, which can also reach large audiences and is often combined with more traditional marketing methods. media advertising The promotion of goods, services, or brands to a wide audience through channels of mass communication. Print advertising appears in hard-copy formats such as magazines, newspapers, brochures, leaflets, postcards, and flyers. Although digital advertising is now the dominant way to reach large audiences, print advertising remains an effective means of attracting consumers, especially in publications with a wide circulation and with

TMP-0784.text: mailings to a narrowly targeted audience. An ad in Runner’s World magazine can reach more than a million athletes. And a housepainter can target new homeowners with a postcard advertising their services. Beyond targeting possibilities, print advertising offers a tangible presence that cannot be clicked away from; flexibility in formats, placements, and sizes; and opportunities to advertise in reputable publications that enhance brand image. Disadvantages include time lags between ad creation and publication, difficulty in tracking ad impact, and high costs for ads in prominent publications.

TMP-0785.text: Logan Bowles/Getty Images For big money, you can reach a big audience with media advertising. An ad during the Super Bowl will cost millions of dollars—and reach more than a hundred million viewers. Broadcast advertising uses television, radio, and other broadcast media to reach a wide audience with promotional messages. Although broadcast advertising has the potential to reach millions, it can be very costly. For instance, a 30-second ad during the Super

TMP-0786.text: Bowl costs around $8 million. Some broadcast advertising is far less expensive. A business on a tight budget can place ads on local television stations for a few thousand dollars each—still a lot of money, but more likely to be justifiable for a small business. Outdoor advertising , also known as out-of-home advertising, is advertising that targets potential customers when they are away from home and off their electronic devices. This can include billboards, posters, flyers, and signage on walls, kiosks, buses, taxis, and transit stations. While consumers have control over which newspapers, radio stations, and websites receive their attention, the high visibility of outdoor advertising has the advantage of reaching people who skip or avoid other types of promotions. Other advantages include lower costs than TV advertising, 24/7 exposure, and opportunities for billboards, signs, and even blow-up items of impressive scale. Disadvantages include the time it takes to install outdoor advertisements, the localized audience, and the difficulty of tracking the impact of these ads.

TMP-0787.text: Maurice Norbert/Alamy Stock Photo Guerilla advertising uses creativity and surprise to create memorable promotions, like this advertising for Adidas in Paris. Marketing teams can make their outdoor advertising more exotic with guerilla advertising , an unconventional form of advertising that uses creativity and surprise to

TMP-0788.text: create memorable promotions. A successful guerilla marketing campaign captures people’s attention, generating social media posts and word-of-mouth advertising that broadens brand awareness. In one example, paper towel brand Bounty placed a gigantic melting popsicle in downtown Los Angeles and a huge knocked-over coffee cup in New York City to get people thinking about the cleaning properties of Bounty products. The message was simple and memorable. Guerilla advertising can also be used indoors, as with a flash mob or a 160-foot Diablo IV mural in a French cathedral. AP ® EXAM TIP An exam question might ask you how you would promote a particular product. Be very specific. Unless the question indicates otherwise, identify the type of promotion you would use, and explain exactly why and how you would use it. Personal Selling In some cases, customers benefit from detailed information or a product demonstration. Personal selling is the direct approach of having a salesperson interact with potential customers. Personal selling is valuable to customers when a purchase is

TMP-0789.text: complex or consequential. For instance, buyers of laptop computers and musical instruments will probably appreciate a salesperson who provides insights and shows them how it works. And if you need help choosing paint at the hardware store, someone with expertise will probably be available to give you the answers you need. personal selling The direct approach of having a salesperson interact with potential customers. Personal selling allows the seller to customize communications based on the customer’s apparent needs and preferences. This may include a sales pitch , which is a brief presentation of the product’s value proposition to encourage a purchase. The salesperson receives immediate feedback and can address issues and answer questions as they arise. A good salesperson creates trust and perhaps long-term relationships with customers, which can increase future sales. A relatively high proportion of potential customers are converted into purchasers by personal selling, because tailored conversations and detailed explanations are generally more persuasive than impersonal forms of promotion. sales pitch A brief presentation of a product’s value proposition to encourage a purchase.

TMP-0790.text: FG Trade/Getty Images For purchases of products like paint that raise many questions, personal selling is the answer. Personal selling has its downsides. It is costly for a business to find and train enough salespeople to give every customer personal attention. As an added expense, to incentivize successful personal selling, salespeople typically receive commission

TMP-0791.text: payments that are a percentage of the value of their sales. A real estate agent might earn a commission of $10,000 or more for a $200,000 home sale. For expensive purchases such as homes and cars, the profit earned on each sale is sufficient to justify personal selling, and buyers appreciate the ability to ask questions and receive assistance. There are also some lower-priced items, such as cosmetics and hardware, that involve enough profit and sufficient interest in expertise to warrant personal selling. For products with a small profit margin or few benefits from personal attention, this sales model is inadvisable. Customers have little need for information from salespeople when making routine purchases of groceries, household items like trash bags, and personal care items like toothpaste. And some customers dislike the pressures of personal selling enough to avoid situations where they will encounter that strategy. Sales Promotions A sales promotion is a marketing strategy of offering temporary incentives to attract customers, boost brand awareness, and increase revenue. Sales promotions can also help a business reduce its inventory or prompt faster buying decisions. We will consider seven popular strategies for sales promotions.

TMP-0792.text: sales promotion A marketing strategy of offering temporary incentives to attract customers, boost brand awareness, and increase revenue. 1. Limited-Time Offers A limited-time offer provides a special deal, such as a discount or two-for-one deal, for a temporary period. Limited-time offers create a sense of urgency and scarcity of availability, which ignites a fear of missing out (FOMO). The “limited time” can be a few months, a few days, or even a few seconds. When Pura Vida Bracelets offered customers a 15% discount on their second purchase, notification of the offer appeared on the company website in a pop-up ad with a countdown timer. The very limited time of the offer encouraged visitors to make a quick decision, driven by a sense of urgency.

TMP-0793.text: Sunrise Photos/Alamy Stock Photo Extended description for Black Friday Advertisements The catalog in focus reads 9 HOURS ONLY! Take advantage of our BLACK FRIDAY.

TMP-0794.text: When the clock is ticking on a limited-time offer, customers are motivated to act quickly so as not to miss out on a deal. 2. Daily Deals A daily deal or flash sale is a sales promotion that offers products at a discount for a short period, often a day. Daily deals can boost revenue quickly and help a store sell excess inventory and “out of season” stock. Like limited-time offers, daily deals create a buzz, trigger FOMO, and increase brand awareness by driving a sense of urgency. One of the biggest flash sales of the year is Black Friday Cyber Monday (BFCM), when brands promote products at a discount for a short time. That event generates tens of billions of dollars’ worth of sales in the United States each year. 3. Product Bundling Product bundling entails combining multiple goods or services and selling them for a reduced price. A spa that bundles a massage with a facial for less than the usual price of that combination is bundling. This is a good way to encourage customers to experiment with new products that might become regular purchases. Buy one, get

TMP-0795.text: one free (BOGO) promotions are similar, the difference being that a BOGO promotion involves a single product. 4. Coupons and Promo Codes If your household still receives a newspaper, you’ll probably find coupons inside. And you’ve likely received online coupons and promo codes that you can enter during checkout to receive a discount. Coupons have long been a popular sales promotion because they entice new purchases by both existing and new customers. Coupons and promo codes allow price-sensitive customers to pay less, while being enough of a hassle to dissuade many non-price-sensitive customers from bothering with them. 5. Clearance Sales Clearance sales offer discounts to motivate buyers and relieve retailers of surplus stock. Clearance sales are a popular way to sell off seasonal stock, such as winter coats, holiday decorations, or swimsuits. They give shoppers a sense of urgency because the sales are temporary, and once the goods are sold, stocks will not be

TMP-0796.text: replenished soon. U.S. clothing company American Eagle Outfitters has promoted clearance sales in its emails with the subject heading, “Up to 70% off clearance: THIS. NEVER. HAPPENS.” The company also triggers FOMO by telling customers that the sale is “3 days only ” and “online only .” 6. Free Trials or Samples Free samples of anything appealing are hard to resist. Free trials of services are attractive to potential customers who face uncertainty about the value a service will provide. Costco provides free food samples such as pizza squares, yogurt, and smoothies to customers regardless of whether they purchase anything. Free samples are also effective for lotions, perfumes, and other nonfood items people like to try before they buy. Adding to the power of this approach, as Module 2.2’s discussion of consumer behavior explained, is the obligation to buy that consumers may feel after receiving a free sample.

TMP-0797.text: mauritius images GmbH/Alamy Stock Photo Free samples reduce customer uncertainty about new products and may create a sense of obligation to make a purchase. 7. Contests

TMP-0798.text: Contests draw the attention of consumers who may not be drawn to other types of promotions, but have a competitive flair and appreciate a chance to win something. These sales promotions work well for new products and for brands competing for consumers’ interests in a crowded market. Possible formats include raffles, photo and video contests, instant-win scratch-off cards, sweepstakes, trivia contests, and like to win games in which people are invited to “like” a page or post to win something. IKEA had a scavenger hunt contest on Instagram in which players searched for clues and solved puzzles. Successful social media contests engage a large audience, increase brand awareness, and build a community around the brand. Direct Marketing Direct marketing is the promotional strategy of communicating directly with potential customers through channels that are not face-to-face. It is direct in the sense that communications are directed toward a target audience rather than appearing in media for the masses. The interactions can be through email, telemarketing, phone calls, mailings, text messages, or social media ads targeting specific audiences. The

TMP-0799.text: communications may be personalized using customer data, but in most cases, direct marketing does not involve one-on-one interactions. direct marketing The promotional strategy of communicating directly with potential customers through channels that are not face-to-face. Your household may receive catalogs from Lands’ End, Pottery Barn, or Bass Pro Shops. Those are examples of direct marketing sent to millions of customers, so direct marketing is clearly scalable. It is also relatively targeted, it can be personalized, and businesses can track responses. For example, Lands’ End can track the orders of catalog recipients to measure the results of its mailings. Direct marketing can be less expensive than less targeted mass-media advertising, which makes it appealing to local businesses like restaurants, gyms, or auto repair shops with a limited advertising budget. This approach can help build customer relationships and loyalty for service-based businesses such as plumbers, hair stylists, and real estate agents by establishing ongoing, personalized communications. Direct marketing is also appealing to B2B businesses, because messages can be tailored to decision makers such as managers and CEOs in ways that other promotions cannot.

TMP-0800.text: The disadvantages of direct marketing include the annoyance some recipients feel when they receive commercial emails, calls, or mailings. Many direct marketing campaigns have a high rejection rate because so many consumers disregard the messages. Businesses that lack a clear target audience may be better off with alternative promotions, because mass direct marketing can be perceived as aimless and unappealing. Online and television advertising may be preferable alternatives for businesses that want to reach the masses. Public Relations Public relations (PR) . is a communication process used to protect or improve a company’s public image and build relationships through the media. Public relations specialists generate positive publicity for their clients by producing and distributing press releases, writing speeches, shaping the firm’s messaging, managing scandals and crises, and crafting responses to negative publicity. For example, to promote the launch of a new smartwatch, a tech company’s PR team might arrange a media interview for its chief technology officer with Wired magazine. The PR team would develop talking points, anticipate potentially tricky questions, and coach the executive on how to stay on message.

TMP-0801.text: public relations (PR) A communication process used to protect or improve a company’s public image and build relationships through the media.

TMP-0802.text: HOW WE TURNED PEOPLE’S FRIDGE LEFTOVERS INTO FIVE-STAR MEALS Have you ever looked into a full fridge and thought “nothing to eat”? It’s a common problem. Because of it, millions of perfectly good ingredients end up in the bin. How can Hellmann’s tackle this? We created a unique dining experience in São Paulo: a gourmet restaurant with no food. Instead, we invited people to bring whatever’s left in their fridge to our restaurant. Our celebrity chefs then transformed their forgotten ingredients into five-star meals, proving how Hellmann’s can combine almost anything. And instead of the bill, we surprised people again with a recipe of their meal. But more than just an immersive installation, our restaurant saved thousands of ingredients, inspiring people to see the food in their fridge in an entirely new light. A public relations campaign created for the Hellman’s brand encouraged people to avoid food waste by [OCR unclear] ​

TMP-0804.text: bringing their leftovers to a gourmet restaurant, where chefs transformed them into fancy meals. Although public relations is often confused with advertising, they are not the same thing. Advertising is paid media , meaning businesses pay for space or time in media such as websites and television shows. Public relations is earned media , which means the business does not pay for media coverage, but instead uses compelling stories and persuasion to gain positive coverage from media outlets. Public relations campaigns can spread powerful messages. For example, New York City-based PR agency Ogilvy worked with the Hellman’s brand to launch “The Restaurant with No Food” campaign to highlight food waste, which is often driven by lack of inspiration. People were asked to bring their unused food to a local restaurant, where chefs transformed the produce into 5-star meals. Not only did the campaign publicize the problem of food waste, but it also went viral on social media and received an endorsement from the United Nations. ​

TMP-0805.text: Marketing in the Digital Age LG How have digital marketing tools changed the way businesses engage with customers? Prior to the 1990s, the types of marketing we now encounter daily on phones and computers hardly existed. To reach a sizable audience, a business had few options beyond newspapers, magazines, broadcast media, billboards, and mass mailings. As access to the internet and email expanded, businesses increasingly dodged the expense of traditional advertising by promoting products directly to consumers using websites and email campaigns. Today, most marketing is digital, because it is easily targeted, quickly manipulated, far reaching, and versatile enough to handle video and audio in addition to text and images. This section explores several types of digital marketing and the associated collection of consumer data. ​

TMP-0806.text: Digital Marketing It’s hard to spend any screen time on an electronic device without being bombarded by digital ads. Digital marketing is the use of digital channels to connect with potential customers and promote products or brands. Digital marketing encompasses all of the advertising messages on websites, mobile apps, email, social media, and other digital formats. Digital billboards and kiosks, along with smartphones, laptops, and other portable devices, bring digital marketing to consumers wherever they are. While digital marketing tools can reach around the world, they can also target small segments of customers with personalized messages at a lower cost than traditional advertising. digital marketing The use of digital channels to connect with potential customers and promote products or brands. Online advertising, sometimes called digital advertising, uses the internet to reach audiences that can be broad or targeted groups of potential customers. Online advertising is versatile, enabling businesses to use any combination of text, images, videos, or audio on websites and social media platforms. As an example of how online advertising can work, AdWords from Google allows companies to pay for ads placed within the search engine results page. The business pays Google if someone clicks on ​

TMP-0807.text: the ad, something that is called pay per click or cost per click . Similarly, Google AdSense allows businesses to place ads on other businesses’ websites, blogs, and forums, and those outlets get paid when people click on those ads. High-traffic websites, such as the cat-lover community catforum.com , receive valuable funding from this form of advertising. Social media advertising is a specific form of online advertising that allows companies to reach target audiences while potential customers are engaging with posts or stories on their preferred social media platforms. Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok, among others, enable businesses and influencers to create photo and video promotions that showcase products and demonstrate their uses. Advertisers can provide blanket coverage across several platforms, or target particular demographic groups with ads on platforms popular among those groups. Another way to attract new customers and boost sales is through in-app advertising that appears inside mobile apps. With the typical consumer spending several hours each day on mobile apps, this form of advertising has become increasingly popular for targeting smartphone users, particularly in the music, gaming, and entertainment industries. Examples include ads that take over the screen between levels of a mobile ​

TMP-0808.text: game, banner ads that appear at the top or bottom of a screen, and ads that reward players with an extra life or coins in a game for watching an ad. Successful in-app advertising can engage customers and create a better user experience, but ineffective in-app advertising can serve as an annoyance, leading users to stop using the app altogether. It’s a balancing act. The rise of Netflix and other streaming platforms has increased the use of product placement advertising , which promotes a brand’s products within media such as movies, video games, and music videos. Companies pay to embed their products in subtle, nonintrusive ways to reach a target audience that follows that particular media. Examples include the Starbucks cups that appear frequently in Fight Club and the prominent Honda Odyssey in Deadpool & Wolverine . Digital media has helped product placement become more sophisticated. Techniques such as dynamic virtual product placement enable customized placement for different households, regions, or platforms. For example, households with pizza lovers might see a billboard advertising Domino’s in a movie scene, whereas households with hot dog lovers see a billboard advertising Ball Park Franks. ​

TMP-0809.text: Barry King/Alamy Stock Photo ​ Extended description for Honda The photo shows Hugh Jackman as Wolverine driving a Honda Odyssey and looking toward the audience with an annoyed expression. Ryan Reynolds as Deadpool rides on top of the car with a whimsical pose. A small dog dressed in a Deadpool jumpsuit hangs out of the back window of the car. ​

TMP-0810.text: Product placements such as the Honda Odyssey in Deadpool & Wolverine are commonplace in the film industry. ​ Customer Data Collection Personal selling allows for some small-scale data collection because salespeople can record information about customers and their purchases. Most traditional marketing tools, including television, radio, newspaper, and billboard advertising, provide no such data. Digital marketing is a different story. Digital platforms can track each item a customer clicks on, social media activities, and purchases. With smart devices giving almost everyone access to the internet most of the time, the data collection from online activities has grown by epic proportions. From a marketing perspective, three types of data can be useful: Contextual data allows companies to target ads to people with particular interests and place ads on websites related to their products. Behavioral data provides information on which websites users visit, what searches they perform, and which products they purchase. ​

TMP-0811.text: Relationship data makes companies aware of customers’ purchasing histories, preferences, and contact information. Data can be “big” or “small.” The term big data refers to large, complex datasets that accumulate rapidly and often require advanced analytical techniques for processing. Digital marketing enables the collection of big data. For example, Netflix collects search and watch data from over 300 million users to learn customer preferences, and it uses that big data for targeted advertising. But it’s not just large companies that use big data—small businesses can benefit from it, too. For example, the Point Defiance Zoo & Aquarium in Tacoma, Washington, has analyzed data from the National Weather Service and its own traffic patterns to predict the number of zoo visitors based on the weather. Those predictions help managers make staffing decisions for bad-weather days when visitor traffic is otherwise uncertain. big data Large, complex datasets that accumulate rapidly and often require advanced analytical techniques for processing. In contrast, small data are more bite-sized pieces that are relatively accessible, informative, and actionable without advanced analytics. Some big companies gain

TMP-0812.text: insights about their customers from small data. LEGO, for example, is an industry giant that used small data to steer important decisions. There were initial suggestions from big data that LEGO should make its bricks bigger, because today’s children don’t have the patience or stamina for more time-consuming projects. But when LEGO executives met with young customers, they discovered the opposite: Children get more pride from a challenge, such as using small pieces to create a LEGO structure. In this context, the small data were the observations made while spending time with groups of customers.

TMP-0813.text: Xinhua News Agency/Getty Images ​ Danish company LEGO used small data to determine that children enjoyed playing with small LEGO pieces. Digital marketing and the resulting data collection stretched the boundaries for data analysis. A wise business will consider all available data, big or small, before making key decisions.

TMP-0814.text: The future of marketing holds new frontiers. For example, companies had long tailored their online content for search engine optimization to help their websites rank higher in search results. Now, the existence of smart speakers such as the Amazon Echo and the Google Nest is prompting companies to optimize their content for voice searches—for example, by including conversational language and key words that shoppers are likely to use when searching for a product. The growing popularity of smart appliances and wearable technology such as fitness trackers, health monitors, and smart glasses provides new levels of data collection and increasingly targeted and personalized ads. And the potential for artificial intelligence begins with the ability to deliver customized messaging to individual customers, and it has no end in sight.

TMP-0815.text: Module 2.7 Review ​ Learning Goals LG What are the five elements of the promotional mix? ​ After product, price, and place in the marketing mix comes promotion , which is any type of marketing communication used to inform target customers about the product. Promotion is central to any marketing campaign , which is a coordinated effort to publicize a product or build brand awareness and attract new customers. The promotional mix is the set of marketing tools a business uses to communicate with potential customers, build brand loyalty, and increase sales. The promotional mix is made up of media advertising, personal selling, sales promotion, direct marketing, and public relations. Media advertising is the promotion of goods, services, or brands to reach a broad audience through channels of mass

TMP-0816.text: communication. These channels include television and radio broadcasts, print publications, and outdoor advertising. Personal selling is the direct approach of having a salesperson interact with potential customers. A sales pitch is a brief presentation of the product’s value proposition to encourage a purchase. A sales promotion is a marketing strategy of offering temporary incentives to attract customer interest, boost brand awareness, and increase sales. Direct marketing is the promotional strategy of communicating directly with potential customers through channels that are not face-to-face. Public relations (PR) is a communication process used to protect or improve a company’s public image and build relationships through the media. LG How have digital marketing tools changed the way businesses engage with customers? ​ Digital marketing encompasses all marketing efforts that use digital channels to connect with customers and promote products or brands. This includes digital

TMP-0817.text: advertising as well as websites, email, social media, and other digital promotional tools. The term big data refers to large, complex datasets that accumulate rapidly and often require advanced analytical techniques for processing. Digital marketing enables the collection of big data. Small data are tiny bits of data that are relatively accessible, informative, and actionable without advanced analytics. Companies can gain important insights about their customers from both big data and small data. Practice Your AP ® Skills Preparing for the AP ® Exam MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTIONS 1. TMP-0820.text: CASE STUDY GEICO and the Gecko Erika Goldring/Getty Images The GEICO insurance company’s gecko mascot gets around and attracts attention wherever he goes. He and other brand mascots help companies reach a broad target audience. ​

headings.text: CASE STUDY GEICO and the Gecko

TMP-0821.navLabel: CASE STUDY GEICO and the Gecko
TMP-0821.text: When you buy your first car, you will also need your first auto insurance policy. The insurance market is fairly competitive, which means you’ll have a lot of options. You’ll also notice a lot of advertising by insurance companies trying to grab the interest of potential customers like you. If you’re familiar with a gecko that walks on its hind legs and talks with a Cockney accent, the GEICO insurance company has succeeded in catching your attention. GEICO began as the Government Employees Insurance Company in 1936 during the height of the Great Depression. Founders Leo and Lillian Goodwin decided to market auto insurance directly to their target audience of federal employees. Thanks to Lillian’s aggressive marketing, the company had written 3,700 insurance policies and hired 12 staff members within its first year. GEICO enjoyed more good years than bad over the following decades, thanks to careful evaluations of the risks it insured and exceptional customer service. For instance, in the 1980s, the company made telephone access for claims, sales, and service available 24 hours a day, every day of the year. In 1996, the company became a subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway, the highly profitable investment firm owned by legendary businessman Warren Buffett. The ​

TMP-0822.navLabel: CASE STUDY GEICO and the Gecko
TMP-0822.text: new owners wanted to reinvigorate the company with a new marketing campaign, but insurance is tricky to pitch. The value proposition of insurance is generally that customers receive assistance in the event of a calamity, which can be a troubling topic. Allstate uses a comedic take on tragedy in its advertising with a character named Mayhem getting injured by reckless behavior. Many insurance companies dodge discussions of harm and grab people’s attention with a charismatic spokesperson, such as Jake from State Farm or Flo from Progressive, or a mascot. After launching an ambitious national advertising campaign with television ads and direct mail focused on saving money on car insurance, GEICO wanted a new advertising gimmick—and it went with a mascot. In 2000, GEICO’s television ads began featuring a friendly talking gecko with a British accent. The little lizard was a big success. In addition to his popular appearances in broadcast advertising, the GEICO gecko has appeared in online, social media, in-app, print, and outdoor advertising. He even took credit for spray painting billboards in a guerilla advertising campaign in Richmond, Virginia, in 2010. 3 ​

TMP-0823.navLabel: CASE STUDY GEICO and the Gecko
TMP-0823.text: In 2004, the company introduced a caveman as a second unlikely insurance spokescreature. According to the accompanying advertising slogan, using geico.com is “so easy even a caveman can do it.” In 2008, the caveman was voted America’s favorite advertising icon of the year and joined the gecko in the Madison Avenue Advertising Walk of Fame. Other insurance brand ambassadors who are recipients of that honor include Progressive’s Flo and Dr. Rick, Allstate’s Mayhem, Liberty Mutual’s LiMu Emu and Doug, and Aflac’s duck. Like all of the advertising icons discussed here, the gecko and caveman continue to feature prominently in GEICO’s advertising. With their help, GEICO now insures over 28 million cars and employs more than 40,000 associates. APPLY YOUR AP ® SKILLS 1. Who is the target audience for car insurance advertising? 2. TMP-0853.text: Essie Weingarten, founder of Essie Cosmetics, started her nail polish business in 1981 with $10,000 in personal savings and one product: a deep red polish called Bordeaux. Today, there are 250 colors, and the Essie line can be found in over 25,000 salons worldwide. 3 Weingarten initially marketed her product by giving away free samples at New York City salons. 4 She was starting out with a very small slice of a mammoth pie. The global nail care services market was worth over $13 billion USD in 2024. Fifty-five percent of U.S. shoppers spend between $51 and $200 on personal grooming — including products like nail polish — every month. 5 A trip to Las Vegas helped the Essie nail polish line take off. With the idea that casino workers often showed their hands, Weingarten visited each of approximately 100 nail salons in the city to gift them samples of 12 different nail polishes, including Bordeaux. This business-to-business marketing was rewarding for Essie. Within days, every salon Weingarten had visited called to order more of her nail polish. Soon after, Weingarten was fielding calls from nail salons nationally — ten thousand of which placed orders within a year of that Las Vegas marketing trip. Like many would-be entrepreneurs, Weingarten experienced some pitfalls. She did not brand her nail polish with the name “Essie” until 1999, many years after the product

TMP-0854.text: became successful. Branding makes it easier for customers to recognize and remember the products that they adore. It cements the image of a company on a physical product, such as Essie’s nail polish bottles. And until 1988, Essie products were advertised solely through word-of-mouth. 6 While Weingarten believed that this was the best form of marketing, industry trade publications might have enabled Essie to reach a broader target market. In 2005, cosmetics giant L’Oreal first approached Weingarten with an offer to buy the Essie line. Weingarten initially declined to sell, but later changed her mind; her business was growing rapidly and required a new facility to meet demand, and she was reluctant to make the investment herself. The sale of Essie to L’Oreal was finalized in 2010. Weingarten no longer had creative control of the company she started, but her name remains on every bottle of Essie nail polish sold. And the acquisition changed Essie’s business model: Whereas Weingarten had sold her products business-to-business (with salons as her customers), Essie products were soon sold business-to-consumer, expanding into retail outlets like drugstores.

TMP-0855.text: Left: Neilson Barnard/Getty Images; right: Anna Webber/Getty Images Extended description for Essie Weingarten The first photo shows Essie Weingarten standing before a wall displaying different shades of Essie's nail polish in rows. The second photo shows a close-up of a pair of hands holding a bottle of Essie nail polish and applying a neutral shade to another person's fingernails.

TMP-0856.text: Entrepreneur Essie Weingarten, shown here, employed a variety of marketing strategies to get her product into thousands of salons nationwide. 9. Describe the role of marketing in the early phase of Essie Weingarten’s business. 10. Explain both the customer and consumer for the Essie line of nail polish, and describe how this evolved when the business was acquired by L’Oreal. 11. If Weingarten had started her business in the 2020s, what marketing strategies could she have used for expanding the brand? 12. Analyze whether or not the market opportunity for cosmetics is larger or smaller today than when Weingarten was starting off in the 1980s.

TMP-0857.text: AP ® Skills Workshop: Entrepreneurship Preparing for the AP ® Exam What Are the Five Course Skills for This AP ® Course? There are five skills you’ll need to build for this course. Two of them are Business Skills: Concept Application and Entrepreneurship . The other three are Professional and Leadership Skills: Decision Making , Collaboration , and Communication . You will find five AP ® Skills Workshops in this text — one at the end of each of the five units, with each workshop addressing one of the Course Skills. In this workshop, we will focus on Entrepreneurship. Identify Entrepreneurship It is important to understand how a business idea begins and how it evolves. This usually starts with a person having an idea or identifying a need or want, and developing a solution to solve that. If it can be scaled, a business is born out of this idea. Thus, entrepreneurship is the process of creating, launching, and running a new business. Understand Entrepreneurship Understanding how to think like an entrepreneur is crucial for success in this course and on the AP ® Business with Personal Finance exam. Entrepreneurship is the heart of business, as nearly all businesses start with an idea from an entrepreneur. In this AP ® Skills Workshop, we will work to ensure that you understand the concept of entrepreneurship. Let’s start by analyzing the process of entrepreneurship for a startup business.

TMP-0858.text: First, a market opportunity must be identified. Try this quick self-test: Describe the concept of market opportunity. Answer: A market opportunity arises when an entrepreneur or business identifies a product or service that customers want or need. A market opportunity involves a customer problem, need, or want. A business takes shape by offering a product or service that provides a solution for that problem, need, or want. Let’s consider two related examples of a market opportunity that evolved into a viable business. As the United States expanded westward, the long distances that people and goods had to travel presented a problem. Two different solutions emerged. • Solution 1: Railway lines were built to make long-distance travel and trade easier, cheaper, and faster from coast to coast. Entrepreneurs built and maintained the tracks used by trains. This innovation led to many thousands of businesses around the United States becoming dependent on railway entrepreneurs, who solved the problem of long-distance travel in a growing nation. • Solution 2: Henry Ford developed the Ford Model T automobile in 1908. It was not the first car built, but Ford’s factories were the first to use assembly lines, and that innovation made the Model T the first affordable car for millions of customers. Like the railway, the mass-produced automobile solved a transportation problem: It was faster than a horse, and the gasoline-powered internal combustion engine did not require rest breaks even after hundreds of miles traveled.

TMP-0859.text: Bettmann/Getty Images With the Model T, Ford seized on a market opportunity and helped millions of customers become car owners. Let’s test your knowledge again: Explain how these transportation entrepreneurs identified and capitalized on a market opportunity. Answer: Railway entrepreneurs and Henry Ford identified and capitalized on a market opportunity when they developed new innovations and products that solved a problem: People and goods had to travel long distances when the United States expanded westward. Railway entrepreneurs built and maintained the train tracks that made long-distance travel easier and cheaper. And Henry Ford’s

TMP-0860.text: Model T, thanks to Ford’s use of assembly lines, became the first affordable car for millions of customers. So, let’s say an entrepreneur has successfully identified a market opportunity. For a business idea to work, they must also test a business hypothesis. For example, if someone wanted to create an app that would simplify the process of finding a pet sitter or dog walker, they would want to know whether or not there is demand in the target community for such a service. And if there is demand, they would need to learn how much potential customers would be willing to pay. An entrepreneur can then use market research to evaluate a new product’s desirability, feasibility, and viability — whether it provides value, can be offered within existing constraints, and has the potential to be profitable. New product ideas can also be tested using a minimum viable product (MVP) — the simplest version of a new product with just enough features to solve a potential customer’s problem, want, or need. A variety of methods exist to test an MVP, including surveys, interviews, and focus groups. Build AP® Skills Here are two activities to help you build the skills you’ll need to succeed in this course. 1. Activity: Consider what you’ve learned about marketing and entrepreneurship in Units 1 and 2. Using that knowledge, explain the process of how you could build, launch, and market a pet-sitting business in your community. 2. Activity: Apply the 4 Ps of the marketing mix to the business idea you outlined in the first question. What do the product, price, place, and promotion consist of for your business?

TMP-0861.text: Business Canvas Project Application Project-Based Learning Continue your work on the Business Canvas Project that you started in Unit 1 , using prompts 1–4. 1. Identify various quantitative and qualitative data that would be useful to know when marketing to the target demographic of your Business Canvas Project. Note: Your teacher may have you create a survey, interview questions, or other means to gather sources of customer data. 2. Design a concept sketch or prototype of the product (or service) that is the focus of your Business Canvas Project. 3. Explain the significance of price from the four Ps of marketing. How should your business determine the price for its main product or service? 4. Create a 30-second sales pitch that shows the uniqueness of your business idea in your community. Your teacher may have you record the business pitch, deliver it live during a class presentation, or write it down.
